words.gloss: they will not become one's own

literal: Even if protected, they will not become [one's own], those which are not [one's] destiny; having carried and poured out, they will not go away, those which are one's own.
translation: Even if one guards them with care, things that are not destined to be one's own will not remain; even if one carries them away and throws them out, things that are destined to be one's own will not leave.
modern: விதிப்படி நமக்கு உரியவை அல்லாத பொருள்களை நாம் போற்றிப் பாதுகாத்தாலும் அவை நம்மிடம் தங்க மாட்டா; நமக்கு உரிய பொருள்களை நாம் கொண்டுபோய்க் கொட்டினாலும் அவை நம்மை விட்டுப் போகாது.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the absolute power of destiny over material possessions. The author explains that what is not destined to be ours cannot be retained, no matter how much effort we put into guarding and protecting it. Conversely, what is destined to be ours cannot be lost; even if we actively try to discard or throw it away, it will find its way back to us and will not leave. Through these contrasting actions of guarding and discarding, the couplet emphasizes that human effort is ultimately subordinate to the laws of destiny.
